anti_overlap: Does not cover behavioral political science or voter research (ANES panel data, generational cohort analysis) — that is fd-political-behavior-trajectory.
Does not cover political identity as tribal signal or the identity-vs-position distinction in cultural studies — that is fd-political-identity-tribal-signal.
Does not cover game-design craft for politics-coding without mockery — that is fd-procedural-politics-craft.
decision_lens: Which structural option (α/β/γ/δ) best models the sociological finding that political identity is a cluster of social identities rather than a set of issue positions — and what does each option require the downstream procedural engine to know about politics that real people don't consciously know about themselves?
focus: Whether politics-coding should be one field or two (or three): apply political sociology's empirical account of how political identity actually clusters in real populations — Putnam on social capital, Skocpol on civic organizations, Mason's 'Uncivil Agreement' on identity-party sorting — to evaluate Options α through δ and determine which structural choice best models real political identity formation without encoding a position-map the engine must maintain
name: fd-political-sociology-axis-structure
persona: Apply the perspective of a political sociologist steeped in Putnam, Skocpol, Lilliana Mason, and the ANES panel-data tradition — they care about whether the axis structure reflects how political identity actually forms (as a cluster of social identities, not a chosen position), measure success by whether the structural choice produces character types that map onto recognizable sociological phenomena (the culturally-conservative economic-progressive; the economically-precarious habitual-Democrat; the post-Tea-Party disaffiliated), and flag any structure that requires the engine to maintain a coherent left/right position-map that political sociology shows is not how real people carry politics.
review_areas: Lilliana Mason's core finding in 'Uncivil Agreement' (2018): Americans have become politically sorted such that party, ideology, race, religion, and geography now align rather than cross-cut — producing high 'social identity consistency' rather than 'issue consistency.' Evaluate Option α (posture-only) against this finding: if social identity consistency is the dominant empirical phenomenon, does a posture-only axis (true-believer / disaffected / gradualist / etc.) capture enough of the sociological signal, or does it systematically miss the identity-cluster structure that Mason documents? A true-believer DSA-organizer and a true-believer talk-radio conservative share a posture but belong to entirely different social identity clusters — does Option α produce characters whose politics is legible without naming the cluster?

Putnam's bowling-alone thesis and Skocpol's research on civic engagement collapse: political identity in the post-civic-organization era is no longer formed through union halls, lodge halls, and civic associations but through mediated networks. Assess whether this generational change in political-identity formation is captured by the formative × current trajectory design: the Unc formed in the civic-organization era (UMWA hall, VFW post, Knights of Columbus) carries a different political substrate than the Unc formed in the platform era (Facebook group, podcast audience, Reddit thread). Does the politics axis need a formation-mechanism modifier, or is this adequately carried by the media-era axis already?

The ANES/Pew 'party identification' measurement debate: political scientists distinguish between 'strong partisan' (affective identity), 'weak partisan' (nominal affiliation), 'independent-leaner' (implicit partisan who denies it), and 'true independent' (rare; genuinely ambivalent). Assess the 8-value draft against this empirical distribution: 'true-believer' and 'traditionally-loyal' together may map onto 'strong + weak partisan' (≈70% of population), while 'disaffected' may map onto 'independent-leaner.' Does the draft's probability distribution (traditionally-loyal 25%, vocationally-absorbed 20%) match the sociological distribution — and if it departs from it, is that departure deliberate?

Option γ (posture + tribal-cluster, two axes) requires the engine to maintain a tribal-cluster vocabulary. Assess the sociological viability of this: political sociology has repeatedly found that tribal clusters are historically contingent (the Solid South flipped; the working-class-Democrat coalition broke), and that any tribal-cluster vocabulary will have a rapidly decaying shelf life. A game designed today with tribal-cluster values ('NPR-liberal,' 'talk-radio-conservative') will read as dated within 5-8 years as media ecosystems shift. Evaluate whether this is a reason to prefer Option α (posture-grain is more durable) or whether it is manageable (tribal-cluster values can be updated without structural change).

Skocpol's research on the Tea Party and its successors documents that political mobilization often happens through pre-existing civic and religious networks rather than through ideological conversion — the Tea Party was not a new political coalition but an activation of an existing organizational substrate. Assess whether 'traditionally-loyal' adequately captures this network-loyalty-activation pattern, or whether it conflates two different phenomena: (a) the Unc who is loyal because he never questioned his formation, and (b) the Unc who was activated by an organizational network and now holds strong positions he experiences as obvious common sense. These are sociologically distinct types.

The 'cross-pressured voter' in political sociology (Berelson, Lazarsfeld, Gaudet in 'The People's Choice') is the person whose social identities point in different directions — the union Catholic who is economically-Democratic but culturally-conservative. Assess whether the 8-value draft can produce cross-pressured Uncs: does a `vocationally-absorbed` Unc (IBEW: economically-union, culturally-conservative region) generate a recognizably cross-pressured character, or does the value flatten him into a single coherent stance? Cross-pressure is one of the most sociologically prevalent political conditions — if the draft cannot generate it, that is a coverage gap.

severity_examples.condition: If the review recommends Option γ and the tribal-cluster values are baked into the enum, the game's politics-coding will require active maintenance as the vocabulary of political tribes changes. A character described as 'NPR-liberal-coded' in 2026 may carry different connotations in 2031 as NPR's audience and reputation shift. The sociological finding that tribal coalitions are historically contingent means this is not a hypothetical risk but an expected maintenance burden.
severity_examples.scenario: Option γ requires maintaining a tribal-cluster vocabulary that becomes a political liability as media ecosystems shift

severity_examples.condition: If a posture-only axis produces characters whose politics is too abstract to recognize (the player sees 'vocationally-absorbed' and cannot infer anything specific about how this Unc relates to political events), the axis fails its recognition goal. The sociological finding that cross-pressure is common means the axis must be able to generate it — but if posture-grain is too abstract to carry tribal flavor, cross-pressure becomes invisible rather than characterologically interesting.
severity_examples.scenario: Option α (posture-only) cannot produce cross-pressured Uncs whose politics is legible to players

severity_examples.condition: If Skocpol's organizational-network-activation pattern and Putnam's inherited-civic-identity pattern both map onto 'traditionally-loyal,' the value is doing double sociological duty: the Unc who votes Democrat because his grandfather was a Democrat is sociologically different from the Unc who was activated by the Tea Party organizational network and now holds positions he experiences as always having been obvious. Both are 'loyal' in surface but have different identity-formation dynamics and different susceptibility to political realignment.

success_hints: Test the structural choice against the Mason sorting finding: does the chosen structure produce characters whose politics is a cluster of social identities (identity-consistent) rather than a set of deliberate positions? Values or structures that require the character to 'have a position' on issues fail this test.

Apply the ANES distribution check: does the draft's probability distribution produce a realistic population of political types, or does it over-represent articulate/engaged politics (true-believer, oppositional) and under-represent the silent-majority types (traditionally-loyal, vocationally-absorbed) that empirical surveys consistently show are the norm?

Evaluate each structural option's shelf-life: which option requires the least vocabulary maintenance as political coalitions reorganize over the next decade? Posture-grain (α) should be more durable than tribal-cluster-grain (β) — but confirm this with concrete examples.
task_context: Reviewing the proposed politics-coding axis for Unc Rancher's procedural character generator — specifically evaluating the Options α through δ structural question (one field vs. two vs. three) through the lens of empirical political sociology, assessing which structure best models how political identity actually forms in real populations without requiring the engine to maintain a position-map or tribal-cluster vocabulary that political sociology shows is historically contingent.
